title: VIP:::Mastering Visual Field Interpretation: From Retinal Nerve Fiber to Occipital Cortex
summary: A comprehensive guide to interpreting Automated Static Perimetry (SAP) and Kinetic Perimetry. This poster integrates the Hodapp-Parrish-Anderson criteria, neurological localization, and clinical pearls for diagnosing glaucoma and neuro-ophthalmic pathologies.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Scope
sections.content: Visual Field (VF) testing is the quantitative assessment of the 'island of vision in a sea of blindness' (Traquair). It measures differential light sensitivity across the retina. In clinical practice, Automated Static Perimetry (SAP), primarily using the Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) or Octopus, is the gold standard for monitoring glaucoma and neurological vision loss.

rows: Heijl-Krakau method: stimuli in blind spot. High FL suggests poor gaze tracking.
'Trigger happy' patient. Increases sensitivity abnormally; produces 'white scotomas'.
Patient fails to respond to brighter stimuli where they previously saw dimmer ones. Common in advanced glaucoma.

branches: Mean Deviation (MD): Overall depression or elevation compared to age-matched normals.
Pattern Standard Deviation (PSD): Measures focal loss; highlights 'hills and valleys' in the island of vision.
Visual Field Index (VFI): Percentage of normal age-corrected sensitivity; weighted toward the center.
Glaucoma Hemifield Test (GHT): Compares 5 mirror-image clusters in upper vs lower halves.

sections.title: Total vs. Pattern Deviation Maps
content: Total Deviation (TD): Highlights all points deviating from the norm. Includes media opacities (cataracts) and refractive errors.
Pattern Deviation (PD): Filters out generalized depression (like cataract) to reveal localized defects (like glaucoma).
Clinical Rule: If TD is worse than PD, consider cataract. If they look identical, the loss is likely purely focal.

branches: Nasal Step: Respects the horizontal raphe.
Arcuate (Bjerrum) Scotoma: Connects blind spot to nasal raphe, arching over fixation.
Paracentral Scotoma: Small focal island within 10 degrees of fixation.
Temporal Wedge: Rare; signifies damage to nasal fibers.
Altitudinal Defect: Loss of an entire upper or lower hemifield.

rows: Usually monocular; respects horizontal midline if vascular.
Respects the vertical midline; 'Crossing fibers' damaged.
Worse symmetry as you move posteriorly; Wernicke's pupil.
'Pie in the Sky'; Meyer's Loop involvement.
'Pie on the Floor'; Baum's Loop involvement.
High symmetry; may have Macular Sparing (dual blood supply).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Interpretation Protocol
content: Step 1: Verify Patient Data (Name, Age, Refractive correction - use +3.00D trial lens for presbyopes).
Step 2: Check Reliability (FL <20%, FP <15%, FN <20%).
Step 3: Analyze Global Indices (Look at MD for severity and VFI for rate of change).
Step 4: Examine the GHT (Normal, Borderline, or Outside Normal Limits).
Step 5: Review Deviation Maps (Identify patterns: Arcuate, Nasal Step, Hemianopia).
Step 6: Correlate with Clinical Findings (Disc cupping, IOP, neuro-imaging).

sections.title: Red Flags: When the Field is Unreliable
content: Cloverleaf Pattern: Patient stops responding mid-test (Fatigue or Malingering).
High False Positives: 'White scotomas' on the grayscale; patient is over-eager.
Learning Effect: Significant improvement between the first and second test.
Rim Artifact: A ring of depression caused by the trial lens frame being too far from the eye.

branches: Optic Disc Drusen: Can mimic arcuate scotomas.
Retinal Branch Artery Occlusion: Sudden altitudinal loss.

sections.title: Recent Advances in Perimetry
content: 10-2 Testing in Glaucoma: Essential for 'Central Island' monitoring in advanced cases or early macular involvement.
SITA-Faster: Reduces test time by 50% compared to SITA-Standard without significant loss of data quality.
VR-Based Perimetry: Portable headsets (e.g., Olleyes, Heru) allowing for home-based monitoring.
AI/Deep Learning: Algorithms now predicting progression faster than traditional GPA (Guided Progression Analysis).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always check the 'Blind Spot' on the grayscale to ensure it's in the correct hemifield (Left vs Right eye).
A 'Nasal Step' of 10 degrees or more is highly suspicious for early glaucoma.
In neurological cases, 'Respecting the Vertical' is the most important feature.
Never diagnose based on one field; look for reproducibility across at least two sessions.

sections.title: Monitoring Progression (GPA)
sections.content: Guided Progression Analysis (GPA) uses a 'baseline' of two tests. It looks for consistent decreases at specific points (Probability symbols). Three triangles (filled) indicate 'Likely Progression,' while two open triangles indicate 'Possible Progression.' Always correlate the VFI slope to estimate the 'Rate of Loss' over time.
